bounded_statement: Within case:46f08f48dfee5b1142a4 only: the exact two-sided binomial test in workflow/analysis.py treats all 24 bout rows as independent trials (18 UV picks of 24, reported p = 0.0227, null rejected), even though data-description.md designates colony_id as the independent-unit column and states that the three rows per colony are related rather than free-standing. Each of the 8 colonies therefore enters the row-independent binomial procedure three times. Collapsing to one outcome per independent unit (6 of 8 colonies UV-majority) gives an exact two-sided binomial p ≈ 0.289, so the report's stated rejection of the null at alpha = 0.05 is not supported by an analysis at the authorized independent unit.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description itself states 'One trial is: one row', and the workflow follows that trial definition exactly; this could be read as authorizing the per-bout test. However, the same document designates colony_id as the independent-unit column and declares rows sharing a colony_id to be related, and a trial definition does not confer the independence the binomial procedure requires, so this does not overturn the finding.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: trial defined as one row, but independence explicitly denied for rows sharing colony_id

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about its assumption and discloses the full per-colony breakdown, so nothing is hidden; but disclosure does not repair the test, and the disclosed breakdown itself evidences the within-colony dependence that invalidates the 24-trial assumption.

The report's own per-colony table shows strong within-colony clustering of picks (five colonies at 3/3 UV, one at 0/3), inconsistent with the independent-trials assumption and material to the result: at the colony level only 6 of 8 colonies are UV-majority, giving exact two-sided binomial p ≈ 0.289 (2 x 37/256), which does not reject the null at alpha = 0.05.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show the row-level test is harmless by re-running the analysis at the authorized independent unit. First I verified the reported statistic is internally correct: with 18 successes in 24 trials at p0 = 0.5, the exact two-sided p is 2 x 190051/2^24 ≈ 0.0227, matching the report, so the discrepancy is not a computation error. Then I aggregated to one outcome per colony: colonies C01-C06 are UV-majority (C06 at 2/3) while C07 and C08 are white-majority, giving 6 of 8 UV-majority colonies and an exact two-sided binomial p = 2 x (28+8+1)/256 ≈ 0.289 > 0.05; pooling raw visit counts within colony gives the same 6-of-8 split. I also checked whether the picks could plausibly be independent despite the shared colony label: the per-colony distribution (five colonies at 3/3, one at 0/3) is strongly overdispersed relative to independent Bernoulli(0.75) trials, confirming within-colony correlation. Every attempt to rescue the reported rejection at the colony level failed, so I could not falsify the issue.

root_cause: analysis.py computes a per-row UV pick for every bout and passes n_uv and n_bouts (24) directly into scipy.stats.binomtest, so each colony's three correlated bouts are counted as three independent Bernoulli trials; the workflow never aggregates to the colony level or otherwise models within-colony dependence, inflating the effective sample size from 8 independent units to 24 rows and producing the anticonservative p = 0.0227.
